public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 572

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/572](https://www.erdosproblems.com/572)
- [Er64c] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in graph theory. Theory of Graphs and its
  Applications (1964), 29-36.
- [BoSi74] Bondy, J. A. and Simonovits, M., Cycles of even length in graphs.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1974), 97-105.
- [LUW95] Lazebnik, F., Ustimenko, V. A. and Woldar, A. J., A new series of dense graphs
  of high girth. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1995), 73-79.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos572

/--
Show that for $k\geq 3$
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;C_{2k})\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{k}}.$$

This problem is #46 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_572 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + 1 / (k : ℝ)) ≤
        (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph (2 * k)) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos572

review.notes:
No mathematical defect found in the sole declaration, Erdos572.erdos_572. It agrees with the lower-bound conjecture in Bondy–Simonovits, Remark 1: the positive constant and sufficiently-large-n threshold may depend on k. The real exponent, ordinary (not induced) cycle containment, and finite extremal maximum have the intended meanings. Scratch Lean checks compiled without errors or warnings, including equivalence with existence of a sufficiently dense cycle-free graph, expansion of the eventual quantifier, and boundary checks. The retrieved community database records problem 572 as open, consistent with the category.

Access limitation: erdosproblems.com/572 repeatedly returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; its live wording and remarks could not be inspected. Mathematical verification therefore used the cited primary literature, with the separate database supplying the status cross-check.
